items.title: Show HN: Blackgit – use Git to only download those cared files
items.contentSnippet:
Git is supposed to be bad at handling mono repos especially where there are many binary files like game projects repo, and also there are no permisson settings, but are important in game development. BlackGit's cli client lets you download only cared files through sparse-checkout(initially not even the default root files) with a mini agent to use natural languages to manipulate the repo, and blackgit's server serves a file level control layer as a proxy to upstreams(github/gitlab)

items.title: Show HN: A website that tracks US food prices every day
items.contentSnippet:
The US Department of Agriculture (USDA) publishes daily food price data for about 290 commodities on:
- what growers were paid at shipping point
- what buyers paid at the big city wholesale markets
- what prices supermarkets advertised in their weekly ads
This data comes out as dozens of separate text reports and PDFs, one per market, with no history and no way to see how prices change over time.

items.title: Show HN: VisionOS 27, iOS 27 object tracking demo – placing objects eyes closed
items.contentSnippet:
I was very excited when visionOS 2 added object tracking two years ago, but there was significant lag that made it unsuitable for real-time placement of objects to match targets.
With this year's visionOS 27 and iOS 27 object tracking updates (primarily high frame rate tracking and more accurate tracking via extended mode training), I put together an open source demo so I can place objects on target with my eyes closed.

items.title: Show HN: Combinators in Array Languages
items.contentSnippet:
Raymond Smullyan’s "To Mock a Mockingbird" book's aviary of combinator birds implemented in APL-derived languages and the problem implementing the Sage bird (Fixed Point or Y combinator) in an eagerly evaluated language.
Newer APLs support lazy evaluation.  My eager language has a workaround for this.   The Z combinator is the standard strict-language fix: wrap the self-application in one extra function layer (λv. x x v), so the recursion is a value (a delayed call) rather than an executing expr

items.title: Show HN: Snagr – abandoned checkout emails for Polar
items.contentSnippet:
I sell digital products with Polar. When someone opens checkout and leaves, Polar doesn’t keep that lead in a useful way for me.
Snagr captures the buyer details at checkout and sends a follow-up email so they can finish payment.
Built it for myself. In the last 30 days it recovered $269.76 for me.
Would love feedback from other Polar / indie sellers and if they would love to see something similar for other Merchant of Records

items.title: What Makes Dual Enrollment Actually Work: Robust Student & Family Support & Career Connection
items.contentSnippet: The third installment in our four-part series with Britebound moves beyond course design to ask a harder question: who is responsible when a student struggles? This post makes the case that robust dual enrollment requires named staff, early drop windows, family scaffolding, and mentors who open doors to careers students have never had reason to imagine. For district leaders building or scaling concurrent enrollment programs, this is the support infrastructure blueprint you have been looking for.
